result.headline: Terrain blocking is the most likely cause, mainly for Three's signal [los_three].
result.explanation: Your area has strong mobile speeds overall, averaging 133.6 Mbps locally and 137.1 Mbps within 1 km [speed_cell][speed_1km], so coverage is generally good. The nearest mast site is about 0.1 km east and serves EE, O2 and Vodafone, confirmed by Ofcom's licence register [nearest_site]. EE, O2 and Vodafone have clear lines of sight to their nearby sites [los_ee][los_o2][los_vodafone]. Three's nearest site is about 0.19 km south, but its line of sight clears the ground by less than 1 m, so trees or buildings could still block it [los_three]. Earlier diagnoses found no similar issues nearby [prior_diagnoses], and high test numbers suggest busy use rather than a current capacity problem because speeds remain well above the UK median [usage_per_head][speed_cell].

rule_based.label: Based on data, not yet reviewed by agents
rule_based.rule: Operators ranked by line of sight from this point to their nearest identified site (clear, then marginal, then blocked); clear lines by distance, obstructed ones by how far the ground rises above the line.
rule_based.text: Likely best network here: Vodafone, with a clear line of sight to a site 0.1 km east (confirmed by Ofcom's licence register). Also a clear line: EE (0.1 km), O2 (0.1 km) and Three (0.2 km).

limitations: Sites are approximate; antenna heights assumed where not confirmed; Ofcom figures are area-level, not exact for this address.
Causes are inferred from public data, not confirmed: operators' network data is not public.
Ookla speeds are quarterly aggregates with no time-of-day detail; congestion can only be inferred.
No address-level Ofcom coverage; Ofcom figures are for the whole constituency and are predictions.
Mast sites are approximate (crowd-sourced OpenCelliD, OpenStreetMap, Ofcom's licence register) and incomplete, so 'no sites found' is weak evidence.
Line of sight uses a surface model (trees and buildings included) and mostly assumed antenna heights; blocked means a weaker signal, not no signal.

critiques.reason: The belief correctly captures the nuance: Three's line of sight is marginal (<1 m clearance, assumed antenna height, crowd-sourced site) so local clutter could block it [los_three], while EE, O2 and Vodafone have clear lines (8 m+ clearance, Ofcom antenna heights) [los_ee, los_o2, los_vodafone] and all speed measures are well above the UK median [speed_cell, speed_1km, speed_neighbours]. Confidence 0.30 is appropriate given the weak evidence for Three's LOS.

No earlier diagnoses exist within 10 km [prior_diagnoses], while current speed tests are abundant and show strong performance [speed_cell, speed_1km, speed_neighbours]. The belief rightly notes speed tests do not directly measure signal strength. Confidence 0.25 fits the limited diagnostic history.

Usage per head is unusually high (38.6 vs UK median 3.6) [usage_per_head], yet download speeds in the cell, 1 km radius and neighbouring cells are all far above the UK median [speed_cell, speed_1km, speed_neighbours]. The belief acknowledges the high usage but correctly concludes capacity is not currently strained. Confidence 0.20 is appropriate.
